page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-192GB is a high-density instance designed for cloud-native enterprise environments. Built upon KVM virtualization and standard x86_64 architecture, the server runs on AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz across 32 physical cores with single-threaded execution. System memory totals 192 GB, establishing an allocation ratio of 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware security and cryptographic extensions include AES and SHA-NI, alongside standard AVX vector instructions and BMI2 bit manipulation flags.

The instance operates without bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating attached network volumes for persistent storage. Furthermore, it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning external ingress requires supplementary network configurations. Because the 32 vCPUs utilize a shared allocation model, execution cycles share physical host resources, resulting in lower single-core synthetic compute metrics, such as a stress-ng single-core score of 750.49.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution and data processing throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core result of 18078.0 and a Passmark CPU encryption rating of 34702.13. Memory subsystem evaluations reveal an uncached read bandwidth of 125.11 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 55.14 GB/sec, supporting fast in-memory operations. Application-level metrics record 42.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.05 GB/sec static web serving throughput, while Passmark database operations reach 16419.44.

By pairing a substantial 192 GB memory footprint with 32 shared AMD EPYC cores, the server offers favorable resource density for memory-centric, concurrent tasks that do not require dedicated core pinning. It is well suited for distributed in-memory data grids, large Redis and Memcached caching tiers, parallel ETL pipelines, and horizontally scaled microservice backends.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-192GB is a high-capacity, memory-dense virtual machine configured within the Cloud Native family. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 shared AMD EPYC 7542 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz, alongside 192 GB of system memory, delivering a generous 6.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on external network storage for persistent volumes. Benchmark testing shows strong parallel performance, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 18078 and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 234.59 GB/sec, bolstered by native AES cryptographic acceleration. Single-thread synthetic performance shows lower throughput in stress-ng evaluations, reflecting its shared execution model and 2.0 GHz base frequency. Delivering solid memory read bandwidth of 125.11 GB/sec and processing 42.41 million Redis operations per second, this instance is well suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching, batch processing, and horizontally scalable cloud services.
